newsitem.title: USA: Texas tornadoes kill 15, wreck dozens of homes.
newsitem.headline: Texas tornadoes kill 15, wreck dozens of homes.

text.p: At least 15 people were killed and about two dozen more were injured on Tuesday when a string of tornadoes and powerful storms tore across central Texas, tossing cars and homes into the air.

Police said the deadliest tornado, one of several that battered the region throughout the afternoon, killed at least 14 people as it flattened dozens of homes in the small Williamson County town of Jarrell, about 40 miles (60 km) north of Austin.

"We've got 14 confirmed dead," Richard Elliot, the chief deputy sheriff for Williamson County, said at a rural community of mobile homes which was obliterated by the tornado. "We've got nothing left except piles of debris."
Several more people were believed missing, he said.
Rescue workers tried to find victims and survivors in the rubble of at least 50 homes and trailer homes torn to shreds when the tornado roared through at about 3:45 p.m. (1645 EDT) (2045 GMT).
Dozens of cars and trucks were torn into bits, their twisted parts lying in ditches, on open ground or entangled in the wreckage of nearby homes.
One truck was buried under a huge stack of broken lumber, its lights still on. It was not clear whether the driver was still inside.

"I seen the tornado on TV and I called my wife and daughters and told them to get in their cars and run," said Al Clawson, the owner of a nearby garbage recycling plant which was wrecked. At least two of the plant's trucks lay on their sides after being tossed into the air.
The tornadoes, accompanied by baseball-sized hail and torrential rain, hit towns and cities between Waco and Austin, and officials said one Austin resident drowned in flash flooding.
"There is some pretty widespread devastation," Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) spokesman Mike Cox said.

Television pictures showed the huge twister kicking up dirt and debris along Interstate 35, the main highway running north-south through Texas and officials said it stopped all southbound traffic for a while.

A separate tornado ripped part of the roof off an Albertson's grocery store at Cedar Park, just north of Austin. Police there said at least eight people were injured and one person was unaccounted for.
A shopping mall and a housing development in the area were also struck. Officials said it was not known how many people were injured or how many buildings were damaged in those locations.
About 20 miles (30 km) further north of Jarrell, another tornado touched down on the edge of Lake Belton, destroying a city-owned marina and half a dozen boats at Morgan's Point Resort.
Several homes were wrecked in the area. "It has been a very busy afternoon," said John Durham, the coordinator of emergency management services in Bell County.
The storms cut off electricity supplies to about 50,000 homes across the four counties hardest hit, officials said.
The DPS was urging people still at work not to drive home because of the spring storms plaguing central Texas and not to enter damaged buildings.
A tornado watch was posted until 1 a.m (0600 GMT) across central and east Texas and into Louisiana and Arkansas.
